decisions.title: Whether the component repositories are harmonized in place, created anew, or folded in
decisions.best_choice: Harmonize the existing component repositories in place, by hand, one pull request each, the roadmap's nine first, in its order; create none, fold none into Auditonomous. Begin when you judge the scaffold close enough for them, as you judged it for the exemplars on 11 November.
decisions.why: Your later rule, that all repositories mirror the 7lm by hand, is what harmonizing in place does, and the two exemplars came onto the model that way. The specification gives a second work a repository of its own, met by peering; folding in would undo that. New clean repositories would leave each work's history in an archived twin, apart from the new repository's L6. Your 14 September words say create; the roadmap's survey found every needed component already exists. If you meant new repositories literally, choose them instead, archiving the old and deleting none.

decisions.title: Trace committed before actuator release, or a pure one-way carrier
decisions.best_choice: Choose trace-before-release: a discretionary action is enabled only after its record commits. Keep the carrier one-way from the compute side, and print the seal-gated interlock, which holds the enable on the sealed side, as a proposal with its open attack pass and trust regress. Rule the recall policy sealed too.
decisions.why: Trace-before-release is the commitment the definition cannot lose: the ebios architecture draft says that without it auditonomy reduces to after-action logging, condition D of the AUDITONOMY term entry puts the record before the act, and the adjudication says the record, not the audit, is what is made in advance. A pure diode gives no delivery guarantee. The interlock keeps your one-way carrier and the ordering together by moving the enable instead of returning an acknowledgement. It is unbuilt, and its likeliest failure is unanswered. Only a ruling that the record may follow the act would choose the pure carrier.
